course.title: Entrepreneurship and Innovation

clos.description: Analyze data-related problems and market information using logical reasoning and structured thinking to evaluate the feasibility of entrepreneurial ideas.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Project-based learning, case study discussion, guided exercises on data-based market analysis and problem framing.
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Market analysis assignment, short quiz on opportunity evaluation.

clos.description: Participate actively and responsibly in diverse teams, demonstrating initiative and leadership in planning and executing group entrepreneurial tasks.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Collaborative learning, team-based project work, peer feedback, reflective discussion on teamwork and leadership.
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Group project participation rubric, peer assessment, brief individual reflection.

clos.description: Generate innovative, data-driven business solutions by developing a coherent business model, marketing strategy, and financial plan for a new venture.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Design thinking workshops, problem-based learning, mentoring sessions on business model, marketing, and financial plan development.
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Progressive project deliverables (business model, marketing strategy, financial plan), mid-semester project review.

clos.description: Communicate entrepreneurial ideas and findings clearly and persuasively through a structured pitching deck and oral presentation.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Flip classroom with sample pitches, presentation skills practice, mock pitch sessions.
clos.assessmentMethodsRaw: Final pitching deck, final group pitch presentation with Q&A.

topics.title: Topic 1: Introduction of Entrepreneurship and Design Thinking (Idea Development)
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Apply design thinking stages to identify a data-informed problem and generate alternative business ideas. LLO2: Work collaboratively in teams to select and refine one business idea.

topics.title: Topic 2: Business Model (Develop business model for their idea)
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Analyze how the chosen idea creates, delivers, and captures value using a structured business model framework. LLO2: Develop a first version of the group’s business model for inclusion in the pitching deck.

topics.title: Topic 3: Market Analysis (market survey, market size, trends)
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Identify target customer segments and collect basic market data through survey, interview, or secondary research. LLO2: Estimate market size and identify key trends to validate or refine the business idea.

topics.title: Topic 4: Marketing Strategy
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Design a basic marketing strategy (e.g., STP, 4Ps) aligned with the market analysis and business model. LLO2: Translate the marketing strategy into clear, visual elements for the pitching deck.

topics.title: Topic 5: Financial Plan
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Prepare simple revenue, cost, and profit assumptions for the proposed business. LLO2: Build a basic financial projection (e.g., first-year forecast) to justify the business’s viability.

topics.title: Topic 6: Pitching Deck and Presentation Skills
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Organize the complete pitching deck (problem, solution, market, business model, marketing, finance) into a clear narrative. LLO2: Deliver a confident, persuasive team presentation using appropriate verbal and visual communication.

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
